name: Transverse Limb Deficiency-Hemangioma Syndrome

criteria.description: Presence of congenital transverse limb deficiency affecting one or more limbs
Presence of cutaneous hemangioma(s) typically localized near or on the affected limb(s)
Exclusion of other syndromes causing limb deficiencies and hemangiomas

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of congenital transverse limb deficiency plus cutaneous hemangioma(s) localized to affected limb(s), with exclusion of other syndromes
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and based on characteristic limb and skin findings; genetic testing may be used to exclude other conditions.

searchTerms: missing part of limb at birth

pathognomonic.symptomName: Cutaneous hemangioma localized to affected limb
searchTerms: skin blood vessel tumor on limb
localized hemangioma on arm or leg

common.symptomName: Soft tissue underdevelopment adjacent to limb deficiency
searchTerms: soft tissue undergrowth near missing limb
reduced muscle or skin near limb defect
soft tissue deficiency beside limb loss

common.symptomName: Localized skin discoloration or telangiectasia near hemangioma
searchTerms: red or purple skin spots near birthmark
visible small blood vessels near lesion
one limb shorter than the other
additional digits on hand or foot
more than normal fingers or toes
small blood vessel tumors under skin elsewhere
red spots on skin away from main lesion

occasional.symptomName: Mild joint contractures adjacent to limb deficiency
searchTerms: mild joint stiffness near limb defect
slight joint tightness beside limb loss
puffy arm or leg near defect

rare.symptomName: Skeletal anomalies beyond limb deficiency (e.g. rib anomalies)
searchTerms: extra or missing bones outside limb
blood vessel tumors in liver or gut

imaging: Ultrasound or MRI demonstrating soft tissue hemangioma
Possible imaging to exclude visceral hemangiomas
genetic: Genetic testing used to exclude other syndromes
other: Clinical observation of hemangioma morphology and distribution
Physical examination confirming limb deficiency pattern

distinguishingFeatures: Presence of extensive pigmentary skin lesions
Capillary malformations with limb hypertrophy rather than deficiency
Limb constriction rings and amputations due to amniotic bands
History suggestive of amniotic band disruption

redFlags: Rapid growth or ulceration of hemangioma
Signs of visceral hemangioma causing organ dysfunction
references: Orphanet: Transverse Limb Deficiency-Hemangioma Syndrome, ORPHA:2486
Rimoin DL, et al. Principles and Practice of Medical Genetics. 7th ed. 2013.
Kraus FT, et al. Congenital Hemangiomas and Limb Deficiencies. Am J Med Genet. 1985.
